answer: A Sybil defense that bites is a per-identity stake bonded behind proof of personhood: each agent locks a copper-denominated deposit slashed to zero when two identities are linked by shared hardware fingerprint or payout address. The roster is capped and the deposit scales with every extra identity from the same subnet, so a farm of N fakes pays roughly N-squared in locked capital. That capital earns nothing all epoch while honest agents collect the comet reward. Each marginal fake therefore costs more than the yield it captures, which is the pearl of the design.
